title: A routing overlay naming a bare FAMILY still crosses transport when the phase's chain holds a non-default driver of that family — the advisor path has the defect the contract-escalation path just had
summary:
PR #390 fixed the observed instance: llmroute.ApplySoftOverlay now promotes the chain's EXACT entry when the chain already contains ov.CLI, instead of rewriting it through defaultDriverForFamily. That closes the contract-escalation case (chain [claude-p codex], overlay 'codex' -> was dispatching codex-tmux, exit=10 with no tmux). It does NOT close the case where the overlay names a bare FAMILY the chain holds only under a non-default driver: chain [claude-p codex] with overlay 'claude' finds no exact match, falls through to defaultDriverForFamily('claude') = claude-tmux, and moves a headless-configured phase onto tmux exactly as before. That is the ADVISOR overlay path (router model-routing projection), which is where overlay CLIs most often arrive as bare family names.

The reason PR #390 stopped at exact-match rather than adding a family-match rung: the vocabulary is genuinely AMBIGUOUS. 'codex' is both a family name and a registered driver name, so 'promote any chain entry of the same family' cannot be distinguished from 'the operator asked for this specific driver'. Concretely, an operator overlay of 'claude-tmux' against a chain of [claude-p] must NOT be satisfied by promoting claude-p — that would override an explicit transport request with the opposite one. Guessing the semantics under release pressure was the wrong trade; deciding them deliberately is this item.
acceptance: Decide and DOCUMENT whether an overlay CLI is a family selector, a driver selector, or both-with-a-precedence — one sentence in llmroute's package doc, since the ambiguity is the actual defect
RED: an explicit driver-qualified overlay must still win over a same-family chain entry (overlay 'claude-tmux' vs chain [claude-p]) — the case that forbids naive family matching
The advisor/router projection path is covered, not just the contract-escalation path — name the production caller for each
